# exifr local photo metadata runtime
Repository https://github.com/MikeKovarik/exifr
Version 7.1.3; npm gitHead 6cbf6e921688faf7723e1f2e0b9e672d1f0aa21c.
Read 2026-11-04: 1253 Stars, last push2024-03-29, unarchived (root API snapshot).
Official npm registry archive downloaded with urllib and SHA1 matched registry metadata; no npm/install/build/test scripts executed. package declares no runtime dependencies. Build/prerelease invoke Rollup, not executed. Original lite.umd.js (45779 bytes) SHA256 530dbaef11cd9d4d65f108abc159b113580eb3dbd7bc69cd1364e25dd40413f9 unchanged, original full MIT2020 Mike Kovarik, Mutiny.cz retained. Exact-commit GitHub LICENSE actually read and matches original text (line endings not asserted). No claim source build reproduction.
Selected lite UMD contains exifr's JPEG/TIFF/EXIF support, not full package HEIC/XMP/PNG features. Library can support URL readers, but platform supplies only a bounded transferred ArrayBuffer in a local Worker; no URL input/network path exposed. No runtime imports, external assets, bundled fonts or declared third-party runtime dependencies. No eval/new Function or Babel helper attribution found in fixed runtime review. Own worker wrapper is platform code.
Chinese wrapper only JPEG <=5MiB, SOF dimensions <=12000 each /40 million pixels, <=512 JPEG segments, six whitelisted scalar metadata fields <=128 chars. Worker timeout 5s terminated; file read stage deadline 5s. No GPS, serial numbers, MakerNote or arbitrary raw dump; no image upload, map, editing or removing metadata. Output presence is metadata, not authenticity verification. Camera dates may be wrong and carry no timezone. TXT/JSON <=16KiB. Browser tests do not prove every JPEG or real device.

Actual compatibility: global pick (names and numbers) fails in this lite build with undefined iterable. Original artifact unchanged; platform uses local ifd0/exif numeric pick lists, gps/makerNote/userComment false. Local options actually passed known and GPS synthetic images. Before parser, bounded APP1 TIFF structural walk validates endian/type sizes/offset+count boundaries, <=16 directories/depth4/512 entries total/256 each and detects repeated directory offsets; selected text <=1024 encoded bytes, output <=128 chars. GPS directory is not traversed; only pointer range is checked. Synthetic cyclic directory/huge count/bad offset rejected before upstream parse. Full UMD was downloaded to investigate but never used and removed from public vendor; only lite original ships.
